topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter: Green Chile Pipeline delayed 6 months to Feb 2027 — ORCL -3.7%, BE falls in sympathy
topSignals.text: — A regulatory filing by Energy Transfer's Transwestern Pipeline unit (published August 14) disclosed that the Green Chile Project's in-service target date has moved to February 1, 2027, from the original August 15, 2026 deadline. The ~18-mile pipeline is designed to deliver up to 400 Mmcf/day of natural gas to the 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC campus in Doña Ana County, NM. ORCL fell 3.7% to near 52-week lows (~$120–122); Bloom Energy shares declined in sympathy. Oracle insists "Project Jupiter remains on schedule," but this is the third supply-chain setback (first March pipeline rejection, second July 14 land commissioner denial, now in-service delay). September 14 NMED air-quality permit hearing remains set. Seeking Alpha | DCD | Motley Fool | StockTwits

topSignals.title: Texas ERCOT data center grid pause — direct positive for on-site SOFC
topSignals.text: — Governor Greg Abbott directed PUCT and ERCOT to audit all data center projects in the interconnection queue before approving any new grid connections. ERCOT suspended its Batch Zero Large Load classification notifications (previously scheduled August 7, 2026); ERCOT will seek a good-cause exception at the PUCT August 20 open meeting. ~474 GW of pending interconnection requests (90% data centers) are now in limbo. Self-supply projects — SOFC behind-the-meter campuses including Hedgehog Texas (104 MW→1.5 GW, already pre-construction) — are exempted from queue requirements. Per 24/7 Wall St.: "retail sentiment turned bullish in August after Texas paused new data center approvals, read as favorable for onsite fuel cell providers." PUCT August 20 is the next procedural gate. Texas Tribune | Utility Dive | Troutman

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: T-2 days to August 17 hard deadline
topSignals.text: — PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP must submit large-load interconnection tariff filings or compliance responses by Monday August 17. No filings published as of August 15. Monday's submissions will define the regulatory cost structure across ~70% of US load and convert the $5–20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost SOFC LCOE benefit from an estimate to a quantified tariff input. LCOE model update scheduled August 18. FERC RM26-4 | McGuireWoods

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet day August 15. Status unchanged: E3000 G2 platform (>75% FC electrical efficiency, 90% with heat recovery, 23,000 SOEC rapid-cycle validated); ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) in volume production; deliveries underway to key partners. No new announcements. Elcogen

Topsoe (priority): Quiet day August 15. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory hibernated pending H2 demand recovery; CEO Elena Scaltritti since June 1, 2026; FY2026 guidance DKK 7,600–8,400M; SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+. No new SOFC announcements. Topsoe

Other players: Quiet day. No new announcements from FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin. Ceres Power: Goldman Sachs Conviction Buy (168% upside, Aug 13) remains the live catalyst; H1 2026 results (September) is the next company-level event.

Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW, Doña Ana County NM): Green Chile Pipeline delayed to Feb 1, 2027 — see Top Signal #1. Third supply-chain regulatory setback for Project Jupiter. NMED September 14 air permit hearing is the parallel critical-path item; the project can advance the permit process regardless of pipeline status, but construction cannot proceed without a fuel supply solution. Oracle maintains the project is on schedule; market skepticism reflected in ORCL stock near 52-week low. Seeking Alpha | BigGo Finance

Active pipeline carry-forward (unchanged): Nebius/Bloom 328 MW Vineland NJ (confirmed active Aug 12); Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (first data halls H2 2026); Hedgehog Texas 1.5 GW (104 MW Phase 1, pre-construction, self-supply, ERCOT audit-exempt); FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW H2 2026 delivery); Equinix >100 MW (19+ DCs); Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS framework; ECL/PowerCell 300 MW+ H2-ready.

FERC RM26-4 (T-2 days, Monday August 17): See Top Signal #3. No tariff filings confirmed as of August 15. Monday's PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP submissions will activate the $5–20/MWh avoided-T-cost as a live LCOE input for on-site SOFC projects in those footprints. Activate as LCOE model sensitivity lever once filings land; model update August 18.

Texas ERCOT data center grid audit (PUCT August 20): See Top Signal #2. Governor Abbott's directive pauses grid approvals for all new large-load data centers; PUCT August 20 open meeting determines whether Batch Zero Large Load processing resumes or suspension continues. Self-supply (off-grid SOFC) projects are exempted — a structural tailwind for behind-the-meter deployments in Texas. Texas Tribune

Background unchanged: NY EO 62 data center moratorium (50 MW+, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE ≤1.2/ERF ≥10%/15% waste heat from July 2026; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks.

Rolls-Royce SMR (UK): GDA Step 3 completion is scheduled for August 2026 (53-month process that started July 31, 2024). No ONR Design Acceptance Confirmation issued as of August 15. If published this week or next, it marks the first Western SMR cleared for UK construction authorization and is the trigger for Wylfa (three units, Great British Energy-Nuclear). Relevant to UK/European SOFC competitive timeline from ~2035 onward. ONR | GDA process

Background unchanged: 13 hyperscaler nuclear deals totaling >9.8 GW; nuclear 10+ year lead times remain SOFC's primary competitive differentiator for near-term deployment; NuScale VOYGR-12 first units not before 2031; battery LCOE ~$25/MWh unsuitable for 24/7 AI baseload.

Bloom Energy (BE): Stock corrected on August 14 from the ~$391 all-time intraday high (August 12) alongside ORCL on Project Jupiter pipeline delay news; 24/7 Wall St. (August 14) cites a current price of ~$246, implying the close was well below the recent record. Still up significantly YTD. 29-analyst consensus remains Buy; average PT $273.51. RBC Capital Buy, PT $335: "major demand ramp" entering data centers. 24/7 Wall St. PT $251.84. Motley Fool (August 13) analysis on "Is Bloom Energy a Buy, Hold, or Sell After Its 1,920% Run?" concludes that $20B+ backlog and hyperscaler validation are structurally intact but execution risk at elevated valuations is real. 247wallst Aug 14 | Motley Fool Aug 13 | Barchart/RBC
Oracle (ORCL): Down 3.7% August 14 to near 52-week lows (~$120–122) on Green Chile Pipeline delay filing. Motley Fool: "Why Oracle Stock Got Trounced Today." TheStreet | Motley Fool
FuelCell Energy, Ceres Power, SolydEra: Quiet. No new material disclosures August 14–15.

Quiet day. No new SOFC-specific patents or IP filings identified for August 15. Cell/stack-materials: Wiley Chemistry – An Asian Journal (2026) published a concise review of SOFC electrode and catalyst advances, covering power density, polarization resistance, and durability; materials-only scope, not system-level. Wiley Asian J.

lcoe.text: FERC RM26-4 (Monday August 17): PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP tariff filings will define the avoided-transmission-cost input ($5–20/MWh range). Activate as live LCOE sensitivity lever once filings land. Model update scheduled August 18.

Texas ERCOT grid pause (PUCT August 20): If Batch Zero Large Load suspension extends into Q4, adjust Texas on-site SOFC pipeline upside: Hedgehog Texas (104 MW pre-construction, self-supply) competes in an environment where utility-grid competitors are stalled. No direct LCOE model parameter changes; flag for pipeline-volume sensitivity.

Oracle Project Jupiter pipeline delay (Feb 1, 2027): Pipeline delay pushes the fuel supply schedule ~6 months for the 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC campus. If air permit clears September 14, construction may begin with interim supply arrangements or a smaller Phase 1 fuel allotment. No LCOE model update to per-kWh structure; affects aggregate MW-deployment timing in the Bloom Energy backlog model.

BE stock correction from ~$391 to ~$246 (August 14): With BE pulling back ~37% from record high, revise WACC sensitivity band upward toward 10.5–11% (from 10–10.5% active since August 3). Bloom's cost of capital directly affects EaaS $/MWh pricing. Revisit after August 17 (FERC filings) and August 20 (PUCT) catalysts — both are structural positive triggers.

Pending (carry-forward, priority-ranked): (1) FERC RM26-4 PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP filings Monday August 17 → model update August 18. (2) PUCT August 20 hearing on ERCOT Batch Zero suspension. (3) NMED September 14 air permit hearing for Project Jupiter. (4) Bloom 10-Q shipped MW extraction (SEC EDGAR, due September 11). (5) Elcogen E3000 G2 system-level efficiency confirmation at ELCO I production scale. (6) Ceres H1 2026 results (September). (7) Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (October). (8) Rolls-Royce SMR GDA Step 3 completion (August 2026, no ONR announcement yet).
